module_title: Vijayanagara and Bahmani - Administration, Culture, and Foreign Travellers
introduction: This level focuses on the unique administrative mechanisms (Nayankara system) of Vijayanagara, its rich cultural growth, the golden age of Telugu literature, and the accounts left by foreign travellers who witnessed its grandeur. We will also explore the splintering of the Bahmani Kingdom.

core_concepts.title: Nayankara and Ayagar Systems
core_concepts.description: Vijayanagara's provincial administration was run via the 'Nayankara' system (land grants to Amara-Nayakas in exchange for military service), while village administration was managed by the 'Ayagar' system (a body of 12 functionaries).

core_concepts.title: Ashtadiggajas and Literature
core_concepts.description: Krishnadevaraya's court was adorned by 8 great Telugu poets known as 'Ashtadiggajas', with Tenali Rama being the most famous. Krishnadevaraya himself wrote the masterpiece 'Amuktamalyada' in Telugu.

core_concepts.title: Accounts of Foreign Travellers
core_concepts.description: Several travellers visited Vijayanagara, including Niccolo de Conti (Italy), Abdur Razzak (Persia), and Domingo Paes (Portugal). They left detailed accounts of the empire's fabulous wealth and bustling markets.

core_concepts.title: Temple Architecture
core_concepts.description: Vijayanagara architecture is famous for the 'Vittalaswami Temple' (musical pillars) and the 'Hazara Rama Temple'. The construction of 'Kalyana Mandapas' (marriage halls) inside temple complexes was their signature feature.

core_concepts.title: Division of the Bahmani Kingdom
core_concepts.description: In the early 16th century, the Bahmani Kingdom broke up into five independent Sultanates: Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Bidar, and Berar.

important_entities.name: Niccolo de Conti
important_entities.significance: Visited during the reign of Devaraya I; gave a comprehensive account of the city's layout and its festivals.

important_entities.name: Abdur Razzak
important_entities.significance: Visited during Devaraya II's reign. He famously stated that Vijayanagara was one of the most splendid cities in the world, the likes of which 'the pupil of the eye has never seen'.

important_entities.name: Domingo Paes
important_entities.significance: Visited during Krishnadevaraya's reign and compared the size and grandeur of Vijayanagara to Rome.

important_entities.name: Mahmud Gawan
important_entities.significance: An outstanding administrator who expanded the Bahmani empire to its greatest territorial limits and built a famous Madrasa in Bidar.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common trap. 'Ashtadiggajas' (8 Telugu poets) belonged to Krishnadevaraya's court, whereas 'Ashtapradhan' (8 ministers) belonged to the Maratha ruler Chhatrapati Shivaji's court.
Remember the specific pairings: Conti -> Devaraya I; Razzak -> Devaraya II; Paes/Nuniz -> Krishnadevaraya/Achyutaraya.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Conti visited Devaraya 1, Razzak visited Devaraya 2, and Paes visited Krishnadevaraya (K).
Acronym for the five splinter states: Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Bidar, Berar.

exam_strategy_tips: Practice 'Match the Following' questions extensively for foreign travellers and their contemporary rulers.
Be sure to remember Krishnadevaraya's literary works specifically: 'Amuktamalyada' (in Telugu) and 'Jambavati Kalyanam' (in Sanskrit).
